results.question: what's the news today
results.answer:
I'll pull today's date and check the latest headlines.Here's the picture as of Friday, 30 October 2026 (00:57 UTC) — so most of this is from Thursday's news cycle.

## Middle East / Iran war
- **Strait of Hormuz:** Iran's IRGC navy claims three to four oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines while trying to exit the strait via an "unauthorized" southern route with radar/navigation switched off (Al Jazeera live blog, AP, Tasnim, Arab News, 29–30 Oct). Results go to President Herzog on 4 Nov; the Knesset is sworn in 10 Nov.

A Madrid–Seville high-speed train slammed into a stationary train near Toledo on Wednesday morning, killing **at least 68 people** (some counts say 69) and hospitalizing around 100, with 544 people aboard the two trains (BBC, AP, Guardian, DW, 28–29 Oct). The transport minister attributed it to a computer failure followed by human error; Spain declared three days of mourning. It's the country's deadliest rail accident in 13 years and the second fatal crash on that line this year (46 died in January).

- A Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv late Thursday killed one person and damaged buildings (Reuters, 30 Oct).
- A drone strike killed 13 people crowding onto a commuter train in Dnipro (Reuters).

An ally blamed ChatGPT for the letter's wording (Reuters, 30 Oct).

- **El Salvador:** Ex-President Tony Saca was freed after serving a reduced 10-year corruption sentence; El Salvador has deployed roughly 2,000–2,500 troops to Haiti to test Bukele's anti-gang playbook abroad (Reuters).

The Fed held rates steady Wednesday, the ECB paused its hiking cycle, and Q3 US GDP came in above expectations. Oil remains elevated — US crude around $102.75/bbl — with gold near $4,013/oz and markets pricing a possible December Fed hike (FXBus, Kapitales, 30 Oct).

- Greek PM Mitsotakis called the Turkey–Libya maritime deal "blatantly illegal, null and void" (Reuters).

results.question: latest news on the federal reserve interest rates
results.answer:
I'll search for the latest Federal Reserve interest rate news.Let me read the primary sources for details.Let me check the forward-looking expectations for the December meeting.## Fed holds at 3.75%–4%, but the vote was split

**The decision (Oct 28, 2026):** The FOMC voted **10–2** to keep the federal funds target range at **3.75%–4%**, per the Fed's own press release. The range has been there since the Fed's **September 2026** quarter-point increase — which the BBC describes as its first rate hike in three years.

**The dissents:** Governor **Lisa Cook** and Cleveland Fed President **Beth Hammack** both wanted a **25bp hike** to 4%–4.25%, according to BBC and CNBC. Notably, this was Cook's first dissent since joining the Fed in 2022 (CNBC). Dallas's Lorie Logan and Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari, who dissented hawkishly in July, voted with the majority this time (CNBC).

**The statement language:** Inflation "remains elevated," and the Committee said "the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal" (Fed release, via CNBC). Economic activity was upgraded to "expanding at a strong pace" from "solid" in September (CNBC). Inflation has run above the 2% target for more than five years (CNBC).

**Warsh's press conference:** Chair **Kevin Warsh** said politics played "no role" in the decision, which landed days before the **Nov 3** midterm elections (BBC, Yahoo Finance). He also announced a structural change: starting in 2027, one of the Fed's annual meetings will focus "exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy, with neither a vote on the federal funds rate nor a policy statement anticipated," and the number of rate-setting meetings will be reduced from eight (CNBC, Axios).

## Where markets think this goes next

The next meeting is **Dec 8–9**, and the consensus is that a hike is more likely than not:

- Fed funds futures implied roughly **85%–87%** odds of a December hike after the decision (Mitrade, Oct 29).
- Kalshi's prediction market showed **~72%** for a 25bp hike and ~29% for a hold (Kalshi market page, accessed Oct 30).
- Reuters reported on Oct 15 that major brokerages "largely expect" at least one more hike this year, with Citigroup forecasting December.

One caution: sources conflict on whether the Fed published a dot plot this cycle — Yahoo Finance references the dot plot pointing to a December hike, while Mitrade says Warsh declined to offer forward guidance or a dot plot. I'd treat the futures-implied odds as the more reliable signal and flag the dot plot question as unresolved in what I could verify.

**Bottom line:** The Fed is on hold but hawkish — a genuine 10–2 split with both dissenters pushing for tighter policy, an explicit "inflation remains elevated" framing, and markets pricing a December increase as the base case. The main uncertainty is timing and whether the committee moves before or after the midterms.

Sources: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/28/fed-interest-rate-decision-october-2026.html, https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cr15jxzv4w24o, https://www.bbc.com/news/live/ck62ylq5v7v1t, https://apnews.com/article/inflation-warsh-interest-rates-federal-reserve-c06793b0c50641444701d5d098ccc2c8, https://www.axios.com/2026/10/28/fed-warsh-interest-rates-cook, https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/live/fed-meeting-live-updates-interest-rates-held-steady-in-split-vote-warsh-says-politics-played-no-role-ahead-of-midterm-elections-191946928.html, https://www.mitrade.com/insights/more/Central-Banks/fed-holds-two-dissent-december-85-20261029J1055, https://kalshi.com/markets/kxfeddecision/fed-meeting/kxfeddecision-26dec, https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/factboxmajor-brokerages-expect-next-fed-rate-hike-in-december-4951431

results.question: summarize https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model
results.answer:
I'll fetch that page and summarize it.## Summary: Wikipedia, "Large language model"

Note on scope: the page extract I retrieved was truncated — I got the full lead section plus the complete table of contents, but not the body text of the individual sections. So the summary below reflects the article's definition and its structure/coverage rather than detailed findings from each section.

**Definition (lead section)**
- A large language model (LLM) is a machine learning model, typically a neural network, trained on a vast amount of text for natural language processing tasks — especially language generation.
- LLMs can generally generate, summarize, translate, and analyze text across many contexts, and they underpin modern chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Qwen, and DeepSeek.
- Most are based on the transformer architecture. Generative pre-trained transformers (GPTs) are a subtype pre-trained to predict the next word, then often fine-tuned to follow instructions and act as assistants.
- The article cautions that biased or inaccurate training data can reduce output reliability, and notes that a software "harness" can give LLMs memory and tool access (e.g., web search). Benchmark evaluations attempt to measure reasoning, factual accuracy, alignment, and safety.

**How the article is organized (section outline)**
1. **History** — includes charts of training compute (FLOPs) versus publication date for notable models, 2010–2024 and 2017–2024.
2. **Naming**
3. **Dataset preprocessing** — tokenization (including byte-pair encoding), dataset cleaning, synthetic data.
4. **Training** — cost, fine-tuning.
5. **Inference**
6. **Architecture** — attention mechanism and context window, mixture of experts, parameter size, quantization.
7. **Extensibility** — prompt engineering, dialogue/chatbot processing, retrieval-augmented generation, tool use, agency (chaining, model-native reasoning).
8. **Forms of input and output** — multimodality, non-natural languages.
9. **Properties** — scaling laws, emergent abilities.
10. **Interpretation** — mechanistic interpretability, understanding and intelligence.
11. **Evaluation** — perplexity and its measures, benchmarks (datasets, adversarial evaluations).
12. **Limitations and challenges** — hallucinations, algorithmic bias (stereotyping, selection bias, political bias).
13. **Safety** — sycophancy, security (prompt injection, sleeper agents).
14. **Societal concerns** — copyright and content memorization, human provenance, energy demands, denial of service due to scraping, mental health, sentience.

If you'd like, I can pull specific sections (e.g., scaling laws, hallucinations, or safety) in more depth — those would need separate fetches, since the single-page extract hit its length limit.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model

results.question: what happened in tech news this week
results.answer:
I'll check the current date and search for this week's tech news.Today is Friday, October 30, 2026, so "this week" covers roughly Oct 26–30. Let me read the source pages to verify the details.Good material. Let me verify a few of the biggest stories before synthesizing.## Tech news: week of Oct 26–30, 2026

Big picture: this was an earnings-and-model-release week dominated by AI money — Anthropic's IPO filing, three frontier model launches, and hyperscaler results — punctuated by what may be the largest crypto theft ever and a rough stretch of security breaches that some outlets are calling "Black October."

### 1. Anthropic filed to go public (Mon, Oct 26)
The biggest story of the week. Anthropic, PBC filed its S-1 for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker **"ANT"** (Anthropic newsroom; SEC filing). Per CNBC and AP:
- Revenue of **$16.29B** for the first half of 2026, versus $1.2B in the same period a year earlier — roughly 14x growth (AP).
- Cost of revenue $2.38B, implying ~**85% gross margin** (CNBC).
- Still unprofitable: an **operating loss of $693M**, an improvement from $2.1B a year prior (TechCrunch).
- The 335-page filing also carries governance/share-structure details and a risk section warning about AI's existential risks (AP; TechNN).
- AP notes Anthropic was valued at $965B by private investors earlier this year, with reports pointing to $1.5T–$2T at IPO — treat those valuation figures as reported, not confirmed.

### 2. Three frontier models in four days
- **OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra (Oct 26)** — pitched on visual reasoning and precise computer use, with a 1.05M-token context window. Pricing halved to **$1/$5 per million input/output tokens** (vs. $2/$12 for GPT-5.6 Terra), which Artificial Analysis called pushing "the cost efficiency frontier" (OpenAI; Artificial Analysis; Simon Willison).
- **Google Gemini 4 Carbon (Oct 28)** — arrived two weeks after "Argon," with gains in coding and agentic tasks. Notably, **access is restricted to vetted cyber defenders**, at $2/$10 per million tokens; MarkTechPost reports 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro (Front Scoop roundup; Google DeepMind).
- **Mistral Large 4 "Le Chonk" (Oct 29)** — open weights for a **trillion-parameter** model aimed at agentic coding and cyber defense; Mistral claims it leapfrogs Chinese open-weight models (SiliconANGLE, The Decoder, Wired, Fortune via TechNN).
- Also: **Nvidia Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe**, an open 30B MoE model for 40-language transcription/translation (MarkTechPost, SiliconANGLE).

### 3. Earnings: AI capex is the whole story
- **Microsoft (Oct 28, FY27 Q1):** revenue **$92.3B**, +19%; operating income $45.9B; net income $36.6B. Azure revenue was disclosed in dollars for the first time at **$33.2B**, and Microsoft booked **$10B in revenue from OpenAI** commercial arrangements — nearly 11% of quarterly revenue (Microsoft IR; TechCrunch). Tenth straight quarter of record revenue (TechCrunch).
- **Amazon (Oct 29, Q3):** revenue **$201.9B**; AWS beat but the stock sank as AI spending overshadowed cloud growth. Jassy said AWS will be a "$1T business" and that Amazon "may have two trillion-dollar businesses in the next 5–10 years" (The Verge; Fortune; Business Insider).
- **Alphabet (Oct 29):** the AI-search monetization problem finally showed up in results — Google is expanding AI Search ads globally as core ad growth slows (Ars Technica; TechCrunch; The Decoder).

### 4. Binance hack — possibly the largest crypto theft ever (Thu, Oct 29)
Binance paused withdrawals after users reported funds draining from wallets, and confirmed it was investigating a "potential security issue" (TechCrunch). Figures reported vary by source:
- CoinDesk: more than **$5B** exploited, with the hacker wallet holding **$5.7B** (incl. ~$1.5B BTC, ~$900M ETH, ~$1.4B in USDT/USDC).
- Glassnode put it at ~**$5.3B** (Investing.com).
- AP: Binance said crypto firms had **frozen more than $2.5B** by Thursday evening; CZ said it "does look like a hack on Binance."
- Contagion: **Polymarket** briefly paused trading after a third-party partner was compromised and said it would fully reimburse affected traders (The Verge/CNBC).

### 5. A brutal security week
- **41,000+ DHS employee records leaked** via DDoSecrets, including ICE and CBP personnel — names, titles, phones, emails, office locations, and per Wired, members of groups tied to wiretap programs (Wired; CyberScoop; TechCrunch; The Hill).
- Axios framed the Binance incident as the capstone of **"Black October"** — a wave of hacks and AI-discovered bugs triggering fears of a broader crisis.
- Related thread: research showing **open-weight AI models can turn security patches into working exploits faster than users can update** (Hacker News/epoch.ai via TechNN), and Wiz's CTO warning of a coming **"vulnpocalypse"** in the internet's aging code (TechCrunch).

### 6. Hardware and devices
- **Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro** launched with a "PROLED XDR" display — the laptop Steve Jobs once called a bad idea (TechCrunch; The Verge Vergecast).
- **Xreal Aura**: wired Android XR glasses with Gemini, ~$1,279 list with a $1,099 intro offer, shipping November (Google; TechCrunch; Tom's Guide; 9to5Google).
- **Amazon devices**: Echo Time smart clock, redesigned Alexa Home Map (interactive 3D view of smart home devices), new Echo Dot/Echo Studio, and an Alexa Photo Frame (Front Scoop roundup; Gizmodo; TechRadar).
- **Intel** says it's selling every affordable laptop chip it can make, with its CFO "not optimistic about next year in terms of memory" (The Verge).

### 7. Platforms and products
- **Reddit** will force everyone to log in as search traffic dries up; CEO Steve Huffman said Google's AI Mode "does not drive traffic" (TechCrunch; The Verge).
- **Instagram** is paying YouTube creators up to $500K (some $50K) to post to its new long-form "Features" format (Business Insider via The Verge).
- **Google is sunsetting Jules**, its AI coding agent, folding learnings into Antigravity (The Verge).
- **Chrome autofill** can now pull suggestions from Gmail with permission (Google; TechCrunch).
- **Meta** shipped an AI pet app, Waddle World (TechCrunch).

### 8. The data-center backlash is now a political story
Voters in Texas and elsewhere are turning against AI data centers; ~70% of young adults say they don't want one in their town (The Verge; Fortune). xAI is reportedly buying out homeowners in Mississippi who promise not to sue over noise — residents call it "Elonville" (The Guardian; The Verge). Mark Cuban described such deals as "contractual terrorism" (Business Insider). Meanwhile Trump's DOE loaned **$5B to nuclear plants** meant to power data centers (TechCrunch), and TechNN's aggregator headlines flag a **Meta $95B stock offering** for AI buildout and a Musk warning that AI neoclouds face mass collapse — I could not independently verify those two, so treat them as aggregator-reported.

### 9. Quick hits
GM to pay **$220M** over selling driving-habits data (The Verge). Upwind raised **$400M** at a $3.8B valuation after walking away from a Datadog acquisition offer (TechCrunch). Rivian's R2 is already its best-selling vehicle; Kodiak landed its first commercial deal for driverless trucks on public highways (TechCrunch). Deepgram acquired Pipecat-maker Daily (TechCrunch).

**Caveats:** "This week" = Oct 26–30. results.question: latest news on the federal reserve interest rates
results.answer:
I'll look up the latest coverage on the Fed's rate decisions and outlook.Let me pull the primary source and check for anything newer than the Oct. 28 decision.## Fed holds at 3.75%–4.00% (Oct. 28, 2026) — but the bias is toward hiking

**The decision:** The FOMC voted **10–2** to keep the federal funds target range at **3.75%–4.00%**, per the Fed's own statement. This follows September's quarter-point increase — the first rate hike in three years — which ended a long cutting cycle.

**The dissents were hawkish, not dovish:** Governor **Lisa Cook** and Cleveland Fed President **Beth Hammack** both wanted an immediate 25bp *increase*. It was Cook's first dissent since joining the Fed in 2022, notable given the ongoing White House effort to remove her (a hearing is set for early November).

**Statement language:**
- Inflation "**remains elevated**" — above the 2% target for more than five years, with core PCE expected above 3% for September.
- The Committee wants "the **accumulation of more information**" before moving again.
- Growth upgraded to "**expanding at a strong pace**" (from "solid" in September).
- The Fed also said it is continuing its policy of maintaining **ample reserves**.

**Warsh's tone:** Chair Kevin Warsh gave no explicit forward guidance, declined to commit to future moves, and said **financial conditions are not tight** — a strong hint his lean is toward higher rates. He also said politics played "no role" in the hold, five days before the Nov. 3 midterms. Separately, he announced a communications overhaul: starting in 2027, one of the eight annual meetings will focus **exclusively on monetary policy strategy**, with no rate vote or statement (two such meetings by 2028).

**What markets expect next:** The next meeting is **Dec. 8–9**, and pricing puts a quarter-point hike as the base case — roughly **72% (Kalshi)**, **79% (rateprobability.com)**, and **85% (Mitrade)** depending on the venue, with further hikes possible in 2027. A Reuters poll before the meeting found 100 of 100 economists expecting a December hike.

**Market reaction:** The S&P 500 held its gains on the announcement; the Treasury curve **steepened** after Warsh's press conference as bond investors stayed focused on inflation and fiscal risk. (Thursday's tech-led selloff was driven by Alphabet earnings, not the Fed.)

**Bottom line:** This was a "hawkish hold" — a pause for data, not a pivot. The live question is no longer *whether* rates rise again, but *when* and *how fast*.

**Definition.** A large language model (LLM) is a machine learning model — typically a neural network — trained on a vast amount of text for natural language processing tasks, especially language generation. LLMs can generally generate, summarize, translate, and analyze text across many contexts, and they underpin modern chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Qwen, and DeepSeek. Most are built on the **transformer** architecture. **Generative pre-trained transformers (GPTs)** are a subtype pre-trained to predict the next word, then often fine-tuned to follow instructions and act as assistants. The article notes that biased or inaccurate training data can make output less reliable, that a software harness can give LLMs memory and tool access (e.g., web search), and that benchmarks attempt to measure reasoning, factual accuracy, alignment, and safety.
